record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.context_brief: Outer automorphism groups of oligomorphic groups
record.original_question: If G is an oligomorphic group, must the outer automorphism group Out(G) always be profinite?

evidence.quote: Problem 21. If G is oligomorphic, is Out(G) always profinite?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{Sym}(\omega)$ denote the group of all permutations of the countably infinite set $\omega = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$, equipped with the topology of pointwise convergence (where a basic open neighbourhood of the identity consists of permutations fixing a given finite tuple). A closed subgroup $G \le \mathrm{Sym}(\omega)$ is called oligomorphic if for every positive integer $n$, the natural action of $G$ on $\omega^n$ has only finitely many orbits.

For such a topological group $G$, let $\mathrm{Aut}(G)$ denote the group of topological group automorphisms of $G$, and let $\mathrm{Inn}(G)$ denote its normal subgroup of inner automorphisms. The outer automorphism group is the topological group
$$\mathrm{Out}(G) = \mathrm{Aut}(G)/\mathrm{Inn}(G),$$
endowed with the quotient of the topology of pointwise convergence on $\mathrm{Aut}(G)$.

Recall that a topological group is profinite if it is isomorphic, as a topological group, to an inverse limit of finite groups (equivalently, it is compact, Hausdorff, and totally disconnected).

Question: Is it true that for every oligomorphic closed subgroup $G \le \mathrm{Sym}(\omega)$, the outer automorphism group $\mathrm{Out}(G)$ is profinite?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears to remain open. Recent work (Paolini–Nies, 2024) studies automorphism groups of oligomorphic groups and notes that $\mathrm{Out}(G)$ is totally disconnected and locally compact, but does not establish profiniteness in general. No resolution of the profiniteness question for all oligomorphic groups was located.

status_evidence.title: Oligomorphic groups, their automorphism groups, and the complexity of their isomorphism
status_evidence.snippet: Out(G) = Aut(G)/Inn(G) is totally disconnected, locally compact; profiniteness in general is not asserted.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work establishes topological properties of Out(G) for oligomorphic G but does not resolve profiniteness in general.
